title: test-0079-SCI-BIO-CONTROL
passage: Dear Diary, today in biology class, we learned how our bodies and plants manage their complex lives. I was surprised to learn that our heartbeat is an involuntary action, meaning it happens automatically without any conscious control from our brain. We also discussed how nerve impulses travel; they do not jump as electrical sparks across the synapse, but instead, chemicals are released to carry the signal to the next neuron. I used to think signals flowed both ways, but my teacher clarified that information travels in only one direction along a single neuron. We also explored how plants respond to their environment. Unlike animals, plants do not have a nervous system to sense touch; instead, they use electrical-chemical signals. I also learned that plant hormones do not just promote growth; some, like abscisic acid, actually inhibit it. Most interestingly, we discussed how light affects auxin. It does not destroy the hormone; rather, auxin simply redistributes to the shaded side of the shoot, causing cells there to grow longer and making the plant bend toward the light. It is fascinating how these silent, invisible processes keep everything functioning perfectly without us ever having to think about them.
summary: Today in biology class, we learned how our bodies and plants work together. It doesn't destroy the hormone; instead, auxin moves to the shaded part of the shoot, making the plant bend toward the light.
